digest.headline: Les avancées en optimisation des agents autonomes et en raisonnement long-context redéfinissent les architectures LLM et robotiques.
digest.overview: Ce 14 octobre 2026, les publications mettent l'accent sur l'amélioration des performances des modèles d'IA via des mécanismes de récompense dense, des architectures unifiées pour la robotique et la conduite autonome, ainsi que des cadres d'auto-évolution pour les agents. Les travaux soulignent aussi des enjeux critiques comme la confidentialité, la sécurité et l'alignement fonctionnel dans des applications concrètes.

highlights.title: Optimisation du raisonnement long-context et des agents
highlights.text: LongR introduit un mécanisme de renforcement par récompenses denses et une approche 'Think-and-Read' pour améliorer le raisonnement en contexte long, avec des gains significatifs sur LongBench v2. Tev et Agent-Reflex complètent cette tendance en proposant des environnements d'entraînement pour agents long-horizon et des cadres de réflexion proactive, essentiels pour des tâches complexes et résilientes.

highlights.title: Architectures unifiées pour la robotique et la conduite autonome
highlights.text: GreenWAM et AUGUstus unifient prédiction d'actions et politiques dans des modèles fondateurs pour la robotique et la conduite autonome, respectivement. GreenWAM utilise un espace d'action anatomique partagé pour une adaptabilité zero-shot, tandis qu'AUGUstus combine génération d'actions et compréhension via une chaîne de pensée, optimisant latence et sécurité.

highlights.title: Auto-évolution et scaffolds dynamiques pour les agents
highlights.text: Self-Evolving Agent Harness et SEAR formalisent des cadres d'auto-évolution pour les agents, où les scaffolds (prompts, mémoire, outils) sont révisés dynamiquement sans modifier les poids du modèle. Ces travaux analysent les limites actuelles et les garanties théoriques, tout en évaluant l'apprentissage autonome de compétences robotiques dans des environnements simulés et physiques.

highlights.title: Optimisation et sécurité des agents de codage
highlights.text: SWE-MISBEHAVIOR identifie des comportements problématiques chez les agents de codage et propose CODE-KIT pour réduire les violations de fichiers et abus système. PreciseCoder améliore le débogage en combinant récompenses unitaires et corrections sémantiques, réduisant les modifications inutiles tout en maintenant les taux de réussite.

highlights.title: Confidentialité et régulation dans les applications concrètes
highlights.text: La collaboration entre DeepMind et le gouvernement de Singapour illustre l'optimisation de modèles légers (Gemma) pour la détection d'arnaques conversationnelles sans exfiltration de données. Ce projet met en lumière l'importance de l'efficacité et de la confidentialité dans des contextes réglementaires stricts.

digest.trend: Les architectures d'agents évoluent vers une intégration plus poussée de mécanismes de raisonnement, d'auto-évolution et d'optimisation, tout en abordant des défis critiques comme la sécurité, la confidentialité et l'alignement fonctionnel. Les modèles unifiés et les cadres théoriques pour l'autonomie avancée deviennent des piliers pour les applications robotiques et décisionnelles.

items.title: LongR: Unleashing Long-Context Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning with Dense Utility Rewards
items.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a key driver for LLM reasoning. This capability is equally pivotal in long-context scenarios---such as long-dialogue understanding and structured data analysis---where the challenge extends beyond consuming tokens to performing rigorous deduction. While existing efforts focus on data synthesis or architectural changes, recent work points out that relying solely on sparse, outcome-only rewards yields limited gains, as such coarse signals are often insufficient to effectively guide the complex long-context reasoning. To address this, we propose LongR, a unified framework that enhances long-context performance by integrating a dynamic ``Think-and-Read'' mechanism---which interleaves reasoning with document consultation---with a contextual density reward based on relative information gain to quantify the utility of the relevant documents, without evidence annotations. Empirically, LongR achieves a gain of over 9\% on LongBench v2 and consistent improvements on RULER and InfiniteBench, demonstrating robust efficiency in navigating extensive contexts. Furthermore, LongR consistently enhances performance across diverse RL algorithms (e.g., DAPO, GSPO). Finally, we conduct in-depth analyses to investigate the impact of reasoning chain length on efficiency and the model's robustness against distractors.
items.tldr: LongR améliore le raisonnement en contexte long via un RL avec récompenses denses basées sur le gain d'information relative, combiné à un mécanisme 'Think-and-Read' dynamique, avec des gains >9% sur LongBench v2 et une robustesse accrue.

deep_analysis.probleme: Le document aborde le défi de l'amélioration des capacités de raisonnement des modèles de langage (LLM) dans des contextes longs, comme l'analyse de dialogues étendus ou de données structurées. Les méthodes actuelles, reposant sur des récompenses éparses (basées uniquement sur le résultat final), peinent à guider efficacement le modèle pour des tâches complexes nécessitant une déduction rigoureuse sur de longs contextes.

methode.approche_generale: LongR propose un cadre unifié combinant un mécanisme dynamique appelé 'Think-and-Read', qui alterne entre phases de raisonnement et consultation de documents, avec une récompense contextuelle dense. Cette récompense est calculée via un gain d'information relatif, mesurant l'utilité des documents pertinents sans nécessiter d'annotations explicites d'évidence.

details_techniques.mecanisme_Think_and_Read: Ce mécanisme permet au modèle d'intercaler des étapes de réflexion interne avec des accès ciblés au contexte long, optimisant ainsi l'extraction et l'utilisation des informations pertinentes.
details_techniques.recompense_dense: La récompense contextuelle dense évalue la qualité des étapes intermédiaires en quantifiant l'apport informationnel des documents consultés, évitant ainsi la dépendance aux signaux de récompense binaires ou éparses.
details_techniques.compatibilite: LongR est conçu pour être compatible avec divers algorithmes de reinforcement learning (RL), tels que DAPO et GSPO, ce qui en fait une solution flexible et adaptable.

resultats.performances: LongR obtient une amélioration de plus de 9 % sur le benchmark LongBench v2, démontrant une efficacité robuste dans la navigation de contextes étendus. Des gains cohérents sont également observés sur les benchmarks RULER et InfiniteBench.
resultats.analyses_complementaires: Des analyses approfondies révèlent que la longueur de la chaîne de raisonnement influence l'efficacité du modèle, et que LongR montre une robustesse accrue face aux distracteurs présents dans le contexte.

limites.manque_details: Le document ne précise pas les coûts computationnels ou la complexité ajoutée par le mécanisme 'Think-and-Read', ce qui pourrait limiter son applicabilité à grande échelle.
limites.dependance_benchmarks: Les résultats reposent principalement sur des benchmarks spécifiques, et leur généralisation à des cas d'usage réels ou variés reste à démontrer.
limites.absence_comparaison: Aucune comparaison directe avec d'autres méthodes de récompense dense ou d'optimisation de contexte long n'est fournie, ce qui laisse des zones d'ombre sur sa supériorité absolue.

deep_analysis.verdict: LongR mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante combinant récompense dense et raisonnement dynamique, mais son adoption nécessitera des validations supplémentaires sur des scénarios réels et une évaluation de son coût opérationnel.

items.title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
items.summary: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. We present GreenWAM, a world foundation model for robotics, together with the recipe that produces it: (1) a shared anatomical action space that describes 20 robot families, from bimanual arms to dexterous humanoids, in common joint coordinates; (2) joint training on these families in visual, action-conditioned and world-action modes; and (3) policies that split an action expert off the generator. As a world model, GreenWAM attains top-tier trajectory, depth and 3D accuracy on WorldArena 1.0, ahead of every world-action model and video generator in our comparison. As a policy, it scores among the top entries of the RoboTwin 2.0 leaderboard, reaches the highest zero-shot LIBERO-plus success among the compared methods and is competitive with dedicated vision-language-action and world-action policies on CALVIN and LIBERO. We further adapt GreenWAM to a real humanoid, where it succeeds more often than policies adapted from π_{0.5} and from Cosmos 3 Edge, and distill it into a single-step policy for real-time control. Controlled experiments yield three findings: robot specialization improves world prediction and control together; an action expert helps when split off at the start of adaptation; and keeping world-model modes during policy adaptation preserves robustness to scene changes.
items.tldr: GreenWAM propose un modèle de monde fondateur pour la robotique, unifiant prédiction d'actions et politiques via un espace d'action anatomique partagé, avec des performances top-tier sur WorldArena 1.0 et RoboTwin 2.0, et une adaptabilité zero-shot sur LIBERO-plus.

deep_analysis.probleme: Le domaine de la robotique manque d'un modèle universel capable à la fois de prédire les conséquences des actions d'un robot sur son environnement (modèle du monde) et de déterminer les actions optimales à exécuter (politique). Actuellement, les modèles sont souvent spécialisés pour l'une de ces deux tâches et dépendent de formats d'action spécifiques à chaque robot, limitant leur généralisation et leur réutilisabilité.
deep_analysis.methode: GreenWAM propose une approche unifiée via un *world foundation model* pour la robotique, reposant sur trois piliers : (1) un **espace d'action anatomique partagé** décrivant 20 familles de robots (bras bimanuels, humanoïdes, etc.) dans un système de coordonnées articulaires commun, (2) un **entraînement conjoint** sur ces familles en combinant trois modes : *visuel* (prédiction d'images), *conditionné par l'action* (prédiction de l'état futur) et *world-action* (intégration des actions dans le modèle du monde), et (3) des **politiques découplées** où un expert en action est séparé du générateur pour améliorer l'adaptation. Le modèle utilise des architectures adaptées aux données multimodales (vision, action, 3D) et est évalué sur des benchmarks standardisés comme WorldArena 1.0 et RoboTwin 2.0.
deep_analysis.resultats: GreenWAM obtient des performances de pointe en tant que modèle du monde, surpassant les autres modèles *world-action* et générateurs vidéo en précision de trajectoire, profondeur et reconstruction 3D sur WorldArena 1.0. En tant que politique, il se classe parmi les meilleurs sur le leaderboard RoboTwin 2.0, atteint le meilleur taux de succès *zero-shot* sur LIBERO-plus, et rivalise avec des politiques dédiées *vision-language-action* sur CALVIN et LIBERO. Sur un humanoïde réel, il surpasse des politiques adaptées depuis π₀.₅ et Cosmos 3 Edge, et peut être distillé en une politique temps réel. Les expériences contrôlées montrent que la spécialisation par robot améliore conjointement prédiction et contrôle, et que le découplage précoce de l'expert en action optimise l'adaptation.
deep_analysis.limites: Le contenu disponible ne précise pas les détails architecturaux exacts (ex. : taille des modèles, volume de données d'entraînement) ni les défis liés à la scalabilité ou à la latence en conditions réelles. L'évaluation *zero-shot* sur LIBERO-plus suggère une généralisation limitée à des tâches non vues, et la robustesse aux changements de scène pourrait dépendre de biais dans les données d'entraînement. Enfin, l'adaptation à des robots très spécifiques (ex. : prothèses) reste une zone d'ombre.
deep_analysis.verdict: GreenWAM représente une avancée significative pour unifier modèles du monde et politiques en robotique, avec des résultats convaincants sur des benchmarks variés, mais son applicabilité industrielle et sa robustesse à long terme méritent des investigations complémentaires.

items.title: Google DeepMind and Singapore Government collaborate to build fine-tuned AI model for scam detection
items.summary: Learn how Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore uses lightweight on-device Gemma models to intercept conversational scams in private chats with zero cloud data egress.
items.tldr: Collaboration DeepMind/GovTech Singapore pour déployer des modèles Gemma légers et on-device afin de détecter des arnaques conversationnelles sans exfiltration de données. Exemple concret d'optimisation pour l'efficacité et la confidentialité, aligné sur les enjeux réglementaires.

deep_analysis.probleme: Cette collaboration vise à résoudre le fléau des arnaques conversationnelles (scams) en temps réel, notamment via des applications de messagerie comme WhatsApp ou SMS. Ces fraudes, souvent basées sur l'ingénierie sociale, ciblent particulièrement les populations vulnérables et sont difficiles à détecter sans analyse contextuelle des échanges. L'objectif est d'intercepter ces tentatives avant qu'elles ne causent des préjudices financiers ou psychologiques, tout en préservant la confidentialité des données utilisateurs.
deep_analysis.methode: L'approche repose sur des modèles légers de type *Gemma* (famille de LLMs open-source de Google DeepMind) optimisés pour fonctionner *on-device*, c'est-à-dire directement sur les appareils mobiles des utilisateurs. Les détails techniques incluent : (1) une architecture adaptée aux contraintes de calcul et de mémoire des smartphones, (2) un entraînement sur des jeux de données synthétiques ou anonymisés de conversations frauduleuses pour éviter les fuites de données sensibles, (3) une détection en temps réel des motifs linguistiques suspects (ex. : urgence artificielle, demandes de transferts d'argent) sans transmission des données vers le cloud (*zero data egress*), et (4) une intégration avec les API de sécurité des systèmes d'exploitation (ex. : Android) pour alerter l'utilisateur. La solution exploite probablement des techniques de *few-shot learning* ou de *fine-tuning* léger pour adapter Gemma aux spécificités locales des arnaques à Singapour.
deep_analysis.resultats: Les informations disponibles ne fournissent pas de chiffres précis sur l'efficacité du système (taux de détection, faux positifs, etc.). Le communiqué met en avant la prouesse technique d'un déploiement *on-device* avec une latence minimale et une consommation énergétique réduite, ainsi que le respect de la vie privée grâce à l'absence de transmission de données vers des serveurs externes. Aucune donnée comparative avec des solutions existantes (comme les filtres cloud de Google ou les outils bancaires) n'est mentionnée.
deep_analysis.limites: Plusieurs zones d'ombre subsistent : (1) l'absence de transparence sur les performances réelles du modèle (risque de faux positifs/negatifs), (2) la dépendance à des jeux de données synthétiques ou limités géographiquement, ce qui pourrait réduire l'efficacité face à des arnaques évolutives ou multilingues, et (3) les défis liés à l'adoption massive (nécessité de mises à jour fréquentes des modèles pour suivre les nouvelles tactiques des fraudeurs). Par ailleurs, le *on-device* limite les possibilités de mise à jour centralisée et d'amélioration continue via le *federated learning*.
deep_analysis.verdict: Cette initiative mérite une attention critique pour son innovation technique en matière de détection locale et respectueuse de la vie privée, mais son impact réel dépendra de données de performance encore non divulguées et de sa capacité à s'adapter à un paysage frauduleux en constante mutation.

items.title: AUGUstus: Autonomous Driving VLA Model with Unified Generation and Understanding
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models show strong potential for end-to-end autonomous driving by leveraging world knowledge and understanding to excel in long-tail scenarios. However, current VLAs have two limitations: 1) Degeneration into vision-action (VA) models. For low latency, regression/flow-based methods directly generate actions but underuse VLM understanding, causing unsafe, unexplainable actions. 2) Autoregressive high latency. Autoregressive methods sequentially generate chain-of-thought (CoT) and action tokens, fully leveraging VLM understanding, but high latency hinders deployment. To enable low-latency deployment while using CoT to assist action generation, we propose AUGUstus, an Autonomous-driving VLA model with Unified Generation and Understanding. We unify diffusion-based action generation and autoregressive CoT understanding in one model, where understanding only serves generation. Joint CoT supervision preserves VLM spatial understanding in shared representation for safer, more accurate trajectories. AUGUstus-mode orders action generation before CoT, so CoT supervises reliable actions during training while inference needs only action output, enabling low latency. AUGUstus-GRPO, a unified GRPO algorithm, jointly optimizes action and CoT, improving action performance. Experiments show AUGUstus achieves 94.6 PDMS on NAVSIMv1 and 90.7 EPDMS on NAVSIMv2, SOTA planning without scorer module. On nuScenes, it achieves average L2 error 0.27 m and average collision rate 0.05%, best among compared methods. To validate AUGUstus practicality, we train on in-house data with 512 NVIDIA H800 GPUs for ~2 days, evaluate on an internal 1,000 km dataset, and preliminarily deploy on a real vehicle, achieving 12 Hz operation. Project page: https://augustus-ad.github.io
items.tldr: AUGUstus unifie génération d'actions et compréhension par chaîne de pensée (CoT) dans un modèle de conduite autonome, combinant faible latence et sécurité via une supervision CoT préservant la compréhension spatiale, avec des gains de performance sur des scénarios à long-tail.

deep_analysis.probleme: Les modèles Vision-Language-Action (VLA) actuels pour la conduite autonome souffrent de deux limitations majeures : soit ils dégénèrent en modèles Vision-Action (VA) en sacrifiant la compréhension sémantique pour réduire la latence, produisant des actions peu sûres et inexplicables, soit ils utilisent une génération autoregressive de tokens (CoT et actions) qui exploite pleinement la compréhension du modèle mais introduit une latence trop élevée pour un déploiement temps réel.
deep_analysis.methode: AUGUstus propose une architecture unifiée combinant génération d'actions par diffusion et compréhension autoregressive (CoT) dans un seul modèle. L'innovation clé réside dans l'ordre de génération (AUGUstus-mode) : les actions sont générées en premier, puis supervisées par le CoT pendant l'entraînement, tandis qu'à l'inférence seule la sortie des actions est utilisée, réduisant la latence. Le modèle utilise un algorithme GRPO unifié (AUGUstus-GRPO) pour optimiser conjointement les actions et le CoT, améliorant ainsi la performance des trajectoires. La supervision jointe du CoT préserve la compréhension spatiale du VLM dans une représentation partagée, garantissant des trajectoires plus sûres et précises.
deep_analysis.resultats: AUGUstus atteint des performances de pointe avec 94,6 PDMS sur NAVSIMv1 et 90,7 EPDMS sur NAVSIMv2, sans module de scoring supplémentaire. Sur le jeu de données nuScenes, il obtient une erreur L2 moyenne de 0,27 m et un taux de collision moyen de 0,05 %, surpassant les méthodes comparées. Le modèle a été entraîné sur des données internes avec 512 GPU NVIDIA H800 pendant environ 2 jours et évalué sur un jeu de données de 1 000 km, avec un déploiement préliminaire sur véhicule réel fonctionnant à 12 Hz.
deep_analysis.limites: Les détails sur la robustesse du modèle face à des scénarios rares ou adversariaux (ex. conditions météo extrêmes) restent flous. La dépendance à un entraînement massif (512 GPU) et à des données internes limite la reproductibilité. Enfin, l'évaluation sur véhicule réel est préliminaire et ne couvre pas encore des cas d'usage variés ou des environnements complexes.
deep_analysis.verdict: AUGUstus mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante unifiant génération et compréhension tout en résolvant le compromis latence/performance, mais sa maturité opérationnelle et sa généralisabilité restent à prouver.

items.title: Beyond Prompt Count: How Data Shapes Transfer in On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains students using teacher feedback on their own sampled responses, yet how prompt choice shapes transfer across teacher-student pairs remains poorly understood. We systematically study prompt quantity, source, and selection across RL- and SFT-continuation pairs and cross-model settings. We find that OPD can be highly prompt-efficient: a few prompts can approach large-pool performance, with four DAPO prompts matching the observed mathematics score of 3,840 DeepMath prompts. However, prompt utility is relational rather than intrinsic: changing only the teacher can reverse the relative effectiveness of mathematics and code prompts. To characterize these transfer differences, we analyze parameter and functional changes across prompt supports and model pairs. Functional alignment with the teacher varies across supports and target tasks; in continuation pairs, teacher-aligned prediction changes can coexist with weak parameter alignment. Continued OPD on effective supports can restore performance after unfavorable transfer. Finally, targeted selection does not consistently outperform uniform random sampling, and filtering out a source that performs poorly alone yields no consistent gain across three paired support draws. Overall, our results distinguish prompt efficiency from prompt interchangeability and show that effective data choice depends on the teacher-student pair and target capability, with random sampling providing a competitive baseline in the studied settings.
items.tldr: Beyond Prompt Count analyse l'impact des prompts dans la distillation on-policy, révélant que quelques prompts bien choisis peuvent égaler des pools massifs, mais que leur utilité dépend du couple enseignant-étudiant, avec des insights sur l'alignement fonctionnel.

items.title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
items.summary: Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery. To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents. Specifically, Agent-Reflex comprises three stages. First, Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD) injects grounded tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a capability-diverse LLM pool, mines matched success-failure pairs, and summarizes reusable reflection meta-skills. Building on this skill library, we then apply Reflective Supervised Fine-Tuning (ReSFT) that converts each skill into supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery, and user-centric correction, strengthening complementary reflective behaviors. Finally, we propose On-Policy Reflective Policy Optimization (ORPO) to combine agentic reinforcement learning under noisy interactions with reflection-guided on-policy distillation to further elicit proactive reflection. Built on Qwen3-8B, Agent-Reflex reaches 58.6 overall on five long-horizon tool-use benchmarks and 29.1 on AgentNoiseBench, surpassing strong environment-scaling and reflection baselines. Experiments on six challenging agent benchmark suites demonstrate the effectiveness of Agent-Reflex. Further analyses show that Agent-Reflex improves agents' robustness to noise while maintaining stable training dynamics, supporting scalable agent training. Our code is available at https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/Agent-Reflex.
items.tldr: Agent-Reflex introduit un cadre d'entraînement en trois étapes pour renforcer la réflexion proactive des agents LLM via des compétences de réflexion découvertes automatiquement, un fine-tuning supervisé réflexif et une optimisation par RL guidée par la réflexion, améliorant la résilience face aux feedbacks bruyants et aux corrections utilisateur. Pertinent pour les agents LLM et leur optimisation.

items.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
items.summary: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. It is built on a latent-world-first approach that first constructs a latent world: a complete and correct hidden specification of the task domain, workflow, and expected state after each step. Each task is then progressively rendered from this specification into an agent-facing environment, enabling controllable complexity and a natural progress metric. Second, we turn this metric into a training recipe: via progress-potential reward shaping (PPRS), we convert progress into a dense per-step reward that improves training efficiency and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. Training with this recipe yields Tev-27B, which achieves substantial gains on the Agents' Last Exam computing and math sciences domains (ALE-CM), matching GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 at Pass@5. Despite training only on ALE-related data, it generalizes to the Terminal-Bench (TB) 3.0 and 4.0 subsets, surpassing GLM 5.2 and Gemini 3.7 Flash, and reaches Claude Opus 4.8-level performance on middle-horizon tasks such as TB 2.1.
items.tldr: Tev propose Tev-Gym, un dataset d'environnements d'entraînement pour agents long-horizon avec récompenses denses et vérifiables, et une méthode de *progress-potential reward shaping* (PPRS) pour améliorer l'efficacité de l'entraînement. Intéressant pour les agents autonomes et l'optimisation des tâches complexes.

items.title: TacitVLA: Reasoning Vision-Language-Action Models Without Reasoning Latency
items.summary: Textual reasoning before acting has improved vision-language-action (VLA) models, but at the cost of latency: every action conditioned on the reasoning text must wait for autoregressive decoding. We show that actions do not need to wait for or condition on the generated reasoning to benefit from it, because the reasoning supervision already improves the backbone representation. We introduce TacitVLA, a reasoning VLA whose action expert never attends to the reasoning it generates for the current call. On long-horizon tasks where the reasoning text also serves as episodic memory, it can generate each entry during action execution rather than before acting. We evaluate it in a controlled study on four benchmarks spanning manipulation and autonomous driving, memory and non-memory tasks: RoboMME, RMBench, LIBERO, and PhysicalAI-AV. On all four, TacitVLA matches the performance of its explicit-reasoning counterpart at up to 3.4x lower latency, and matches the latency of the same architecture trained without reasoning at up to +17.1% success. In absolute terms, it surpasses the best previously published results on the RoboMME Counting suite (82.7% vs. 66.8%) and RMBench (77.5% vs. 56.5%), and reaches 72.9% on LIBERO-Plus and a 52.5% scene score on the public split of the PhysicalAI-AV closed-loop driving challenge. Project page: https://tacitvla.github.io.
items.tldr: TacitVLA supprime la latence liée au raisonnement textuel dans les modèles VLA en séparant la génération de raisonnement de l'action, tout en conservant les bénéfices du raisonnement. Jusqu'à 3.4x plus rapide avec des performances égales ou supérieures.

items.title: LifeSearch: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents for Real-World Life and Productivity
items.summary: Deep research (DR) agents address open-ended information needs through multi-step reasoning, long-horizon web search, and evidence synthesis. However, existing benchmarks primarily focus on academic research or synthetic tasks, leaving DR agents' capabilities in real-world life and professional productivity settings insufficiently evaluated. To bridge this gap, we introduce LifeSearch, a challenging benchmark comprising 203 Chinese and English tasks derived from real-user query seeds across 7 concrete life and productivity domains. With more than 4,500 hours of human annotation, we construct over 4,000 expert-written, fine-grained rubrics, covering both report-content criteria for coverage and accuracy and concrete criteria specifying values, units, dates, and URLs. We conduct extensive experiments on 12 advanced DR agents under a unified evaluation harness, systematically analyzing their performance patterns and failure modes. We find that even the best-performing frontier agent, GPT-5.6 Sol, achieves a score of only 63.4%, leaving substantial room for improvement on realistic life and professional DR tasks. We select the grading configuration by comparing candidate LLM judges against human rubric labels, and a human ranking study shows strong alignment between aggregate benchmark scores and human judgments (Spearman's ρ= 0.89, Kendall's τ= 0.81). LifeSearch provides a rigorous evaluation framework and foundation for advancing DR agents toward real-world life and productivity.
items.tldr: LifeSearch introduit un benchmark de 203 tâches réelles pour évaluer les agents de recherche approfondie (DR) dans des contextes de productivité et de vie quotidienne, révélant des limites majeures (score max de 63.4% pour GPT-5.6 Sol). Pertinent pour l'évaluation des agents autonomes et leur généralisation.

items.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
items.summary: System one models enable direct, low-latency decision-making. Yet recent practice of predicting an answer from serialized text does not, by itself, respect the structure of a decision problem. We argue that current designs underemphasize four important structural requirements. (i) null-aware: Models should distinguish answer absence from uncertainty among candidates; (ii) permutation-invariant: Reordering alternatives should not change the decision; (iii) option-scalable: Growing candidate sets should not require redefining the output space; (iv) cacheable: Request-independent computation over recurring alternatives should be reusable across requests. We introduce Jeva, a decision-native architecture that addresses these requirements jointly. A shared encoder independently represents the request and each option, while a compact decision stack refines only the request state against immutable option memory. Symmetric aggregation yields permutation-equivariant probabilities; shared scoring accommodates variable-size candidate sets. A separate coverage estimate distinguishes answer absence from candidate competition, enabling explicit null outcomes. Request-independent option representations and layer projections support reuse across newly assembled sets. These mechanisms unify Choice, Noul, and Score outputs. Across evaluations, Jeva combines strong typed-decision performance with near-perfect null detection and no decision flips under any tested permutations. It scales to thousands of candidates and substantially reduces latency through cross-request reuse without changing decisions.
items.tldr: Jeva propose une architecture native pour les modèles de décision (system one) respectant des contraintes structurelles (null-aware, permutation-invariant, option-scalable, cacheable), avec un encodeur partagé et un stack de décision compact, optimisant les décisions à faible latence. Très pertinent pour les architectures LLM et l'optimisation des systèmes décisionnels.

items.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
items.summary: Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. Every primitive requires a round of LLM reasoning over the full interaction history, so the cost of an episode grows with the number of primitives. We find this reasoning largely redundant: once a sub-goal is chosen, its primitives follow a routine already prescribed by memory. We present ChunkAct, which introduces action chunking to agentic robotics. Online, a single call launches a chunk of chained primitives, which executes autonomously and returns control only upon failure. Offline, ChunkAct compiles the memory into these chunks, so execution is memory-free at test time and the planner is reserved for decisions that require reasoning. LLM computation therefore scales with the number of decisions rather than the number of primitives. On LIBERO-Pro, ChunkAct improves task success by 5.0 points over the state of the art in agentic robotics while requiring 2.9x fewer LLM calls, 4.4x fewer input tokens, and 2.3x fewer output tokens.

extra.authors: Bingxin Xu, Wenrui Bao, Xinxin Liu, Jiawei Zhou, Yuzhang Shang, Emilio Ferrara

items.tldr: ChunkAct optimise l'efficacité des agents robotiques basés sur LLM en regroupant des actions en chunks exécutables sans appel répété au modèle, réduisant les coûts de calcul de 2.9x tout en améliorant le succès des tâches de 5 points sur LIBERO-Pro.

items.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
items.summary: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning. Compared with frontier LLM Agents and agentic frameworks spanning both text-based and latent methods, HybridAgent consistently improves performance by 10.4%, while delivering 35.5%-54.7% token reduction, 1.8x-2.6x faster inference, and 2.7x-3.7x cost savings. Code and data are available at https://github.com/togethercomputer/HybridAgent.

extra.authors: Jiaru Zou, Yunzhe Qi, Sirui Chen, Federico Bianchi, Shang Zhu, Pan Lu

items.tldr: HybridAgents combine raisonnement latent et textuel dans un cadre unifié, permettant des transitions dynamiques entre modes pour optimiser l'efficacité et la transparence des agents, avec des gains sur 11 benchmarks mathématiques et scientifiques.

items.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Robots are increasingly autonomous in task execution, yet their improvement remains largely human-driven. This study investigates Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), in which physical experience guides lasting updates to both a robot's capabilities and its improvement procedure, making subsequent improvement more effective across tasks. Physical RSI faces challenges from noisy observations, continuous dynamics, costly trials, and irreversible consequences. We present an L0-L5 framework that differentiates capability-level from meta-level updates and within-task from across-task gains, reserving L5 for independently verified recursive gain. We study existing methods around harness adaptation and model training, alongside safety and control mechanisms that govern execution and successive updates. Our analysis reveals that, despite substantial progress in self-improvement, the surveyed literature does not yet demonstrate Physical RSI as defined by our framework. We identify research priorities in reliable feedback, causal attribution, safety preservation, and benchmarking, outlining a path toward robots that autonomously improve how they learn while ensuring safety. The GitHub repository for Physical RSI is available at https://github.com/SAIL-Research-Lab/Physical-RSI.

extra.authors: Hai Zhou, Fan Yang, Zeyi Chen, Lejun Zhang, Chenyang Fu, Jianping Li

items.tldr: Cadre théorique (L0-L5) pour la *Physical Recursive Self-Improvement* des robots, distinguant mises à jour de capacités et méta-apprentissage, avec analyse des limites actuelles. Fondamental pour l'autonomie robotique avancée, mais encore prospectif.

items.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
items.summary: Harness self-evolution revises an agent's software scaffolding, including prompts, memory, workflows, and executable components, while keeping model weights fixed. We formalize a feedback-driven process in which accepted revisions persist across runs. The framework separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms. It distinguishes changes to interpreted state from revisions to tools and code, repository-level control logic, and plugin composition. We characterize search through evolutionary optimization and examine its reliability through continual PAC-learning. Under explicit assumptions, the analysis yields an expected generalization bound, a retention bound conditional on historical regression budgets, and a high-probability admission rule using fresh, independent validation data. We examine how persistent harness revisions affect knowledge sharing and organizational workflows, with implications for scientific reliability, physical safety, and institutional accountability. Cases from prior work illustrate model--harness co-design, distributed execution, and plugin reuse. Reliable deployment requires continual validation as task distributions and evaluators change, with independent safeguards for learning, runtime privileges, and consequential actions. We provide a comprehensive 66-page discussion of related work, theory, algorithms, evaluation, applications, and the broader impact of Harness RSI, together with continuously updated code and supplementary materials, at https://github.com/zgcagi/Harness-RSI.

extra.authors: Chuyang Wei, Haoxiang Guan, Minghang Zhu, Kexin Zhou, Jiyan He, Xiren Zhou

items.tldr: Ce travail formalise un cadre d'auto-évolution pour les agents IA, où les scaffolds (prompts, mémoire, outils) sont révisés dynamiquement via un processus de feedback sans modifier les poids du modèle. Le cadre inclut des garanties théoriques (bornes de généralisation, règles d'admission) et analyse les implications pour la fiabilité, la sécurité et la responsabilité institutionnelle, avec des exemples concrets de co-conception modèle-scaffold.

items.title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics
items.summary: Frontier language-model agents can now improve robots on their own: they write control code, test it, and keep what works as skills and memories for the next task. We introduce SEAR (Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics), a framework and benchmark built around two questions. Is the agent really learning, or just trying more often? And does what it learns still help on new tasks, in a new simulator, and on a real robot? The framework runs an agent in three modes: it writes code that becomes the policy (code-as-policy), acts live in the control loop (agent-as-policy), or works as a researcher that fine-tunes a vision-language-action model (auto-research). The benchmark adds controls that separate retained experience from repeated attempts, familiar tasks, privileged simulator state, larger budgets, and luck. Across seven frontier language models, 330 simulated and five physical tasks, and over four years of agent runtime, we highlight three findings. First, the learning curve of a robotic agent depends both on the overall time budget and the task difficulty relative to model capability. Harder tasks make longer sessions worthwhile; on easier tasks, re-rolling short attempts does just as well. Second, control code and shared routines transfer across tasks and simulators, while task-specific solutions do not. On a real robot, we observe a performance gap between agent-designed practice and novel human-designed scenes. Third, different models evolve more effectively in different ways. Some do best acting live, others writing code first. And a text-only model keeps pace with a comparable multimodal one: perception helps with error assessment, but agentic reasoning and tool use can matter more. We release the benchmark and codebase to support future research.

extra.authors: Xinyi Wang, Bangzheng Li, Hanyu Wang, Lin Zhang, Andrea Yaoyun Cui, Zhenggang Tang

items.tldr: SEAR évalue l'apprentissage autonome de compétences robotiques par des agents IA frontaliers, distinguant l'apprentissage réel de la répétition d'essais. Sur 330 tâches simulées et 5 physiques, le cadre montre que la courbe d'apprentissage dépend du budget temps et de la difficulté de la tâche, avec des insights sur la généralisation et l'efficacité des frameworks auto-évolutifs.

items.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Long-horizon agents accumulate progress in persistent task state, yet repeatedly process interaction histories describing how that progress was achieved. This raises a natural question: can long-horizon context instead be organized around reusable progress rather than the history that produced it? In this paper, we introduce CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime that organizes continuation around reusable task objects. Rather than treating compressed histories or reconstructed accounts of progress as the primary basis for continuation, CarryOn builds a context view from continuation carriers, complementary execution context, and a live tail of recent interactions. A core challenge is keeping this reusable basis valid after its surrounding history is retired: how can CarryOn update the basis without reconstructing the full representation at every fold? CarryOn maintains carrier records across folds, revising affected records against bound evidence and applicable environment checks while carrying forward unaffected records and jointly updating execution context. Experiments on OSWorld 2.0 and BrowseComp-Plus show improved gains of 5.8% and 7.0% while reducing total token usage by 51.9% and 22.9%, respectively. Project page: https://ethannju.github.io/carryon

extra.authors: Yuchen Lu, Julian McAuley, Lei Zhang

items.tldr: CarryOn propose une architecture d'agents long-horizon basée sur des objets réutilisables (context carriers) pour structurer le contexte de continuation, réduisant la redondance des historiques tout en améliorant l'efficacité (gain de 5.8-7% sur OSWorld 2.0 et BrowseComp-Plus) et en diminuant l'usage de tokens.

items.title: PreciseCoder: Faithful and Generalizable Debugging Beyond Unit-Test Rewards
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) from unit tests is the common recipe for post-training code models, but a unit test only asks whether the final program passes. We analyze what this unit-test-only reward teaches a model during debugging and find that, while it raises pass rates, it also teaches the model to edit more and to hallucinate bugs in code that is already correct. We introduce PreciseCoder, a training algorithm that augments the unit-test reward with a signal for semantically verified, localized edits, which correlates with smaller edits and higher pass rates. On 4B, 9B, and 27B models, PreciseCoder reduces the average number of edit lines from 7-15to 3 at a pass rate on par with unit-test-only training. Trained only on single-line bugs, PreciseCoder can generalize to repository-level program repair, where it resolves more issues with smaller patches. Its precision also transfers from weaker to stronger models: given the reasoning trace of a 9B PreciseCoder model, frontier models such as GPT-5.6 Sol and Qwen3.8-Max gain 4.6-12.4 points in edit precision with no additional training. Linguistic analysis of the thinking traces shows that our reward encourages the model to reason about individual lines, name the buggy ones, and form consistent bug hypotheses.

extra.authors: Yunkai Zhan, Miaosen Chai, Shangshang Wang, Jike Zhong, Yuqing Yang, Deqing Fu

items.tldr: PreciseCoder améliore le débogage des modèles de code en combinant récompenses unitaires avec des signaux de corrections sémantiques localisées, réduisant les modifications inutiles (7-15 lignes → 3 lignes) tout en maintenant les taux de réussite.

items.title: A Refresh Interval Does Not Fully Specify a Refresh Schedule: Learning-Rate-Dependent Placement in Kronecker-Preconditioned Language Model Training
items.summary: Kronecker-preconditioned optimizers recompute a cached curvature eigendecomposition only periodically, and implementations and adaptive methods control this through the refresh frequency. We show that frequency leaves part of a schedule free: at a fixed number of refreshes, when they occur changes held-out loss at the same compute. Training GPT-style models with the Mousse optimizer across model sizes, we move the middle refreshes of a four-refresh schedule while fixing the first and last. On FineWeb the two placements exchanged rank as the learning rate rose (later placement was better at low rates, earlier placement at high ones), so a single-learning-rate comparison can report either ranking. The reversal held under controls including the published optimizer internals, and placement still mattered at the published refresh density. The learning rate at which the preference flips fell with model size, consistent with a held-out smaller model, and shifted with training length. A spectral-width staleness score predicted the same ranking at every learning rate and missed the reversal. Refresh schedules should be reported in full and compared across the learning rates at which they will be used.

extra.authors: Xinyu Wang, Zhiwei Zhai, Yu Gu, Zijun Yu, Sicheng Lyu, Jingrui Tian

items.tldr: Cette étude démontre que la *refresh frequency* (intervalle de rafraîchissement) des optimiseurs à préconditionnement de Kronecker n'est pas suffisante pour définir une *refresh schedule* optimale : la position des rafraîchissements dans le temps impacte significativement la perte de validation, avec des effets dépendants du *learning rate* et de la taille du modèle. Les résultats soulignent l'importance de rapporter des *schedules* complètes et de les comparer sur une plage de *learning rates* pour une évaluation robuste.

items.title: Knowing the User Is Not Knowing What We Established: Grounding Awareness in Personal Agents
items.summary: Personal-agent memory has largely focused on learning what users know, prefer, and want. However, knowing the user does not necessarily mean knowing what the user and the agent have established together. An assistant's proposal should not become an authorized instruction merely because it is remembered. We introduce Grounding Awareness, the ability to distinguish accepted, unacknowledged, revised, and scoped arrangements when selecting actions. We develop a controlled benchmark to test whether agents can tell the difference between proposals users have accepted and those they have not, and whether they apply accepted arrangements only where appropriate. Across multiple agents and memory systems, we find that strong memory performance does not ensure Grounding Awareness. More surprisingly, providing more complete user information can increase execution of unacknowledged proposals, while persistent memory can cause agents to treat these proposals as if they were user instructions. We trace these failures through memory writing, retrieval, and action selection. Finally, we introduce Grounding Layer, a lightweight, training-free extension that explicitly tracks grounding status and checks consequential actions, substantially improving agent behavior without modifying models or memory systems.

extra.authors: Jiajun Chen, Xinyue Chen, Yicheng Jiang, Hua Shen

items.tldr: L'étude introduit le concept de *Grounding Awareness* pour les agents personnels, soulignant que la mémorisation des préférences/utilisateurs ne garantit pas la compréhension des arrangements établis (acceptés, révisés, etc.). Un benchmark contrôlé révèle que les agents échouent à distinguer les propositions acceptées de celles non reconnues, même avec des systèmes de mémoire performants, et propose une solution légère (*Grounding Layer*) pour suivre explicitement le statut de *grounding* des instructions.

items.title: SWE-MISBEHAVIOR: Benchmarking and Mitigating Boundary Violations in Software Coding Agents
items.summary: We present SWE-MISBEHAVIOR, the first taxonomy and evaluation framework for diagnosing boundary-violating misbehaviors in coding agents. It contains 7.4K human-in-the-loop synthesized samples spanning three layers of agent action space: (i) Code Generation, (ii) File Management, and (iii) System Interaction. Across these categories, SWE-MISBEHAVIOR covers 11 distinct misbehaviors with a fully automated evaluation protocol, including coding-action violations, Create/Read/Update/Delete (CRUD) file misbehaviors, system integrity and abuse violations, and task-goal misalignment. Experiments on state-of-the-art open-source coding agents (e.g., OpenHands, smolagents) reveal substantial misaligned behaviors, including dependency misinterpretation (up to 98.5% of cases), unintended modification of user inputs (50.5%), and silent compromise of environment integrity (53%). Motivated by these findings, we further propose CODE-KIT, a lightweight adaptive framework that combines misbehavior-aware guidelines with novel tools to help agents avoid such failures. CODE-KIT reduces misbehaviors by 52% for smolagents and 34% for OpenHands, while simultaneously improving task completion performance.
items.tldr: SWE-MISBEHAVIOR identifie et évalue 11 types de comportements problématiques (ex: violations de fichiers, abus système) chez les agents de codage, avec un taux d'échec jusqu'à 98.5%. Propose CODE-KIT pour réduire ces erreurs de 34-52%. Essentiel pour la sécurité et la fiabilité des agents autonomes.

items.title: WAVE-0: Bridging VLA Policies and WAMs with Lightweight Latent Future Prediction
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies excel at generalist robotic manipulation but generate actions without explicitly modeling their environmental consequences. World action models (WAMs) incorporate future prediction, yet most rely on costly video generation, while latent alternatives either use predicted futures only as auxiliary targets or infer latent actions from suboptimal visual transitions through costly large-scale video pretraining. We introduce WAVE-0 (World-model-Augmented VLA Execution), a framework that bridges VLAs and WAMs through a lightweight latent world model. By connecting the semantic understanding of pretrained VLAs with explicit future prediction, WAVE-0 allows anticipated action consequences to directly guide action generation. Built on a pretrained VLA, its 257M world model translates VLM-generated latent action plans into predicted future representations that condition the action expert, unifying latent planning, future prediction, and action generation. The world model is trained directly on ground-truth robot actions with a counterfactual ranking objective, requiring neither pixel reconstruction nor large-scale video pretraining. WAVE-0 achieves success rates of 91.47% on RoboTwin 2.0 and 98.7% on LIBERO, along with 88.0%, 61.4%, and 75.0% on LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Pro, and LIBERO-Para, respectively. On real-world tasks, it improves the success rate of π_{0.5} from 38.3% to 73.3%. These results demonstrate strong manipulation performance and generalization across diverse distribution shifts.
items.tldr: WAVE-0 intègre un modèle latent léger pour prédire les conséquences futures des actions dans les politiques VLA, combinant compréhension sémantique et prédiction explicite pour guider la génération d'actions, sans besoin de reconstruction vidéo coûteuse. Pertinent pour les agents robotiques et l'optimisation des politiques d'action.

items.title: ReTerm: Recovery Training for Self-Improving Terminal Agents
items.summary: Terminal agents have shown strong abilities in complex coding tasks. However, they often struggle to recover from errors during long-running execution (e.g., command errors, faulty implementations), eventually leading to task failures. To this end, we present ReTerm, a self-improving terminal agent trained by learning how to recover from its own failed terminal tasks. To support its training, we construct a customized data pipeline and produce ReTerm-10K, a high-quality dataset that provides effective recovery demonstrations for SFT cold start. Furthermore, we propose ReTerm-GRPO, an online RL algorithm that forks from the agent's own failure states to generate multiple independent self-recovery attempts. By learning from whether these attempts successfully complete the task, the agent self-improves through its own recovery experience. Built on Qwen3.5-9B, our ReTerm-9B achieves 34.8% Pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2.0, improving over the base model by 14.6 points. Further analysis shows that our method achieves consistently higher recovery rates across diverse error categories compared with standard GRPO training. All code, data and model are released at https://github.com/twothsnd/ReTerm.
items.tldr: ReTerm améliore les agents terminaux auto-améliorants en apprenant à récupérer des erreurs via un dataset de démonstrations de récupération (ReTerm-10K) et un algorithme RL (ReTerm-GRPO) qui génère des tentatives de récupération à partir d'états d'échec, améliorant significativement les performances sur Terminal-Bench 2.0. Très pertinent pour les agents LLM et leur optimisation.

items.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
items.summary: Visual agents must turn video observations into timely decisions to track progress and choose what to do next. Building on the emerging System One paradigm, we introduce VideoJev, a family of models that cast video understanding and interaction as structured decision tasks. We adapt pretrained multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by replacing autoregressive answer decoding with a shared head that scores temporal intervals and textual options against video evidence. These scores yield event spans or answer choices, unifying temporal grounding and multiple-choice video question answering. This combines the semantic flexibility of MLLMs with efficient decisions that agents can use directly. As an interaction unfolds, new goals and intermediate results prompt further queries about the same visual history. VideoJev therefore reuses visual computation through Cached inference for queries as they arrive and Joint inference for multiple queries in a single forward pass. Across three temporal grounding benchmarks, VideoJev-4B and VideoJev-35B-A3B improve mean mIoU over their backbones by 6.7 and 10.8 points, respectively, with measured inference speedups of 2.8-3.1times. On four video QA benchmarks, both achieve performance comparable to their backbones in Thinking mode, with measured inference speedups exceeding 100times. These results offer a unified, reusable decision interface for composing structured visual judgments into complex, open-ended workflows.
items.tldr: VideoJev adapte les MLLM pour la compréhension vidéo et l'interaction via un système de décision structuré (scoring d'intervalles temporels), avec des gains en mIoU et des accélérations d'inférence (2.8-3.1x). Modèle prometteur pour les agents visuels.

items.title: Back-Translation Still Matters: Leveraging Monolingual Data for Low-Resource Machine Translation with LLMs
items.summary: Pre-trained Large Language Model (LLMs) are effective on many tasks in zero-shot and few-shot settings. For machine translation of low-resource languages, the obvious options are few-shot prompting and fine-tuning on a small parallel set. We ask: what if moderate amounts of low-resource monolingual data are also available? We argue that, rather than continued pretraining, a more effective use of this data is the pre-LLM era technique of back-translation (BT). The current fine-tuned LLM translates monolingual sentences in each language, and the resulting pairs train it in the reverse direction. Updates on the parallel set are interleaved for stable learning. With 1K parallel pairs on Odia and Swahili, BT beats continued pretraining into the low-resource language by 7.7 to 16.4 XCOMET-XXL points in domain. With beam-decoded intermediate translations, it also beats a model with 10 time more parallel data. In-context examples retrieved from the parallel data further improve BT. We also analyze the source, quality and amount of monolingual text. Across five low-resource languages, with Hindi as a high-resource control, and two 3B backbones, BT improves translation into the low-resource language by 16 to 173% XCOMET-XXL over parallel-only fine-tuning. Blind human evaluation on Odia and Sanskrit agrees with the automatic metrics.

extra.authors: Divyanshu Bathla, Parag Singla, Jitin Singla

items.tldr: Ce papier montre que la rétro-traduction (back-translation) reste une méthode efficace pour améliorer la traduction automatique de langues peu dotées, même avec des LLM pré-entraînés. En utilisant des données monolingues modérées, la BT surpasse le fine-tuning direct ou le pré-entraînement continu, avec des gains significatifs (jusqu'à +16.4 XCOMET-XXL points) et une robustesse accrue par rapport à des modèles entraînés sur 10x plus de données parallèles.

items.title: Enabling Token-wise Importance Sampling in Off-Policy RLVR with Proximal KL Regularization
items.summary: Off-policy data in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can arise from asynchronous generation, rollout-training mismatch, and response reuse. Token-wise importance weighting avoids multiplying likelihood ratios across a response but generally biases policy gradients. We prove that, under coverage and local expressiveness conditions, full future KL credit makes the exact proximal optimizer the update's unique stationary policy, even for mixtures of older policies, without full-response weights or a fitted critic. We further establish convergence of continuous-time tabular population updates under persistent coverage and time-varying behavior policies, and a finite-sample reward guarantee for linear logistic models under additional assumptions. These results motivate Proximal KL, a practical off-policy RLVR method that separates the proximal reference from the sampling policy and replaces PPO clipping with bounded future KL credit. Across all seven matched off-policy comparisons on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B, spanning two learning rates, response reuse, and rollout staleness, Proximal KL outperforms GRPO in micro-averaged accuracy over eight math benchmarks by up to 2.58%. A separate on-policy comparison yields comparable aggregate accuracy. In periodic-refresh experiments, Proximal KL avoids the collapses observed in PG and CISPO, exceeds GRPO's training accuracy, and reaches higher accuracy in fewer policy updates. Ablations show that token-wise correction outperforms sequence-level and unweighted controls. With token-wise correction retained, future KL feedback reduces sensitivity to the tested baseline perturbation relative to PPO clipping. A finite future horizon improves AIME24 mean@16 and pass@16 over the full tail, while fixed-policy measurements show that truncation reduces correction variance over the tested horizons.

extra.authors: Hao Bai, Jiarui Yao, Tong Zhang

items.tldr: Propose une méthode d'optimisation hors-policy pour le RL avec récompenses vérifiables (RLVR), basée sur une régularisation KL proximale et un échantillonnage token-wise. Démontre des gains significatifs (jusqu'à +2% en précision) sur des benchmarks mathématiques avec Qwen3, avec des garanties théoriques de convergence et des preuves de biais réduit.

items.title: WorldCast: Distributed Multiplayer World Models
items.summary: Multiplayer world models must generate independently controlled views with consistent representations of both players and their shared environment. Most existing approaches coordinate multiple players through joint multi-view generation, whose cost grows with each additional player. We present WorldCast, a distributed multiplayer world model in which each player runs a local client comprising a video generator and a state model. Using recorded player positions and map geometry during training, the state model estimates the player's position from generated video and control inputs. Clients exchange player states and project them into camera-aligned player state fields that guide where and how other players are rendered. Shared scene state enables clients to reuse one another's generated observations to maintain consistent scene appearance across views. Experiments on Counter-Strike 2 demonstrate WorldCast's consistency, real-time performance, and distributed scalability. The camera-aligned player state field improves player rendering rates by over an order of magnitude over joint-generation methods, while shared scene state improves visual consistency over whole rounds. Each client runs in real time and exchanges only player and scene states, enabling scalable multiplayer generation without a centralized computational bottleneck. Image quality remains stable over hour-long rollouts.
items.tldr: WorldCast introduit un modèle de monde distribué pour environnements multi-joueurs où chaque client génère des vues locales et synchronise les états partagés via des champs de projection, réduisant drastiquement les coûts de calcul et améliorant la cohérence visuelle en temps réel, validé sur Counter-Strike 2.

items.title: What Really Works for Universal Multimodal Embeddings? A Controlled Study of Contrastive Training Strategies
items.summary: Contrastive learning has become the standard paradigm for multimodal representation learning, aligning semantically matched pairs while separating mismatched ones in a shared embedding space. Although various contrastive training strategies have been proposed across negative selection, batch construction, and gradient modulation, their actual effectiveness under controlled, reproducible conditions remains poorly understood. This motivates a fundamental question: Do sophisticated contrastive strategies consistently bring meaningful downstream gains in multimodal embedding learning? To address this, we systematically evaluate representative strategies under a unified benchmarking framework on MMEB. Surprisingly, direct evaluations reveal that most existing strategies offer marginal gains over a standard aligned baseline, with several even degrading overall performance. To uncover the underlying failure modes, we introduce an MLLM-as-a-Judge diagnostic framework that dissects top-1 retrieval behaviors into labeled positives, false negatives (unlabeled valid matches), and hard/easy negative errors. Our systematic analysis yields three key insights: (1) Gradient distortion: Upweighting gradients from high-similarity negatives consistently hurts downstream generalization; (2) Distribution illusion: Wider separation between positive and negative similarity distributions does not necessarily translate to better retrieval performance; and (3) Synergistic training: While false-negative mitigation or hard-batch construction yields limited gains in isolation, integrating hard-negative mining, false-negative mitigation, and hard-batch construction achieves optimal performance, delivering an average improvement of 6.0% on MMEB with Qwen2-VL-2B. Overall, our findings demystify popular contrastive strategies and provide actionable recipes for training universal multimodal embedding models.
items.tldr: Cette étude contrôlée démontre que les stratégies contrastives avancées pour les embeddings multimodaux n'apportent que des gains marginaux par rapport à une baseline simple, avec des insights sur les biais de gradient et les erreurs de négatifs, via un cadre diagnostique MLLM-as-a-Judge.

items.title: EMHO: EMbodied Agent Harness Optimization via Experience Traces
items.summary: Improving embodied agents often focuses on optimizing the underlying model through training, while the surrounding agent harness that controls planning, context, and tool use is typically engineered. We ask whether this harness can instead improve itself directly from experience traces under sparse environmental feedback. We propose EMbodied Agent Harness Optimization (EMHO), a self-evolving framework that keeps the embodied model frozen and iteratively revises its harness by analyzing execution trajectories and prior harness history. EMHO optimizes beyond skills or recovery prompts, modifying how the agent monitors progress, uses vision tools, grounds observations, and responds to failures. To support multiple subtasks with a single harness, we introduce EMHO-Merge, which addresses trade-offs in jointly optimizing a single shared harness across subtasks by using episode-level gains and losses to guide evidence-supported refinement of when and how revised behaviors are applied. We evaluate EMHO on EmbodiedBench across navigation and manipulation tasks, and EMHO consistently improves task success for both Qwen 9B and 27B models. Qualitative analysis shows that EMHO goes beyond recovering from failures and unproductive actions to reshape how the embodied agent interprets and interacts with its environment.
items.tldr: EMHO optimise automatiquement le 'harness' (orchestration) d'agents incarnés en analysant des traces d'expérience, améliorant les performances sans modifier le modèle sous-jacent, avec une approche EMHO-Merge pour gérer plusieurs sous-tâches.

items.title: SHELDON: Reasoning through Dual Search over Hypothesis and Observation Spaces
items.summary: Test-time scaling has enabled LLMs to solve increasingly complex reasoning, discovery, and optimization tasks. However, existing approaches often gather observations while seeking evidence for current hypotheses, then generate new hypotheses conditioned on those hypotheses and their associated evidence. This couples observation discovery to existing hypotheses, favoring local refinements over exploration of unknown hypotheses regions. Inspired by the hypothetico-deductive method (Hempel, 1945) and dual-space models of scientific discovery (Klahr & Dunbar, 1988), we introduce SHELDON, a scientific reasoning harness that separately represents and jointly explores hypothesis and observation spaces. By actively seeking new observations along with new hypotheses, SHELDON can discover observations that its current hypotheses do not explain. These unexplained observations expose gaps in its understanding, motivate new investigations, and guide the generation of hypotheses beyond refinements of existing ones. Across diagnosis, abstract reasoning, and optimization benchmarks, SHELDON outperforms evaluated baselines by up to 26.7 points. Additional analysis shows that SHELDON generates up to 4.5x more novel solutions.
items.tldr: SHELDON propose une méthode de raisonnement par recherche duale (hypothèses/observations) inspirée de la méthode hypothético-déductive, améliorant les performances sur des benchmarks de raisonnement complexe jusqu'à +26.7 points. Approche novatrice pour les agents scientifiques et l'optimisation du test-time scaling.

items.title: Self-Distillation with Verbal Regularization
items.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) trains a large language model using supervision from a teacher instantiated from the same model as the student. The teacher is conditioned on privileged information (PI), such as verified solutions. The student, which does not observe PI, learns from the teacher's next-token distributions along its own sampled responses. However, PI can bias supervision toward shortcut reasoning with limited verification or reconsideration, accompanied by a sharp drop in the entropy of the output distribution. To address this challenge, we introduce self-distillation with verbal regularization (VRSD), which uses system prompts to regulate how the teacher uses PI, thereby encouraging rethinking and exploration to counteract premature commitment. Theoretically, we model prompting as attenuating the influence of PI on the teacher distribution and derive conditions for entropy preservation. Across three models and four tasks, VRSD improves Pass@1 over OPSD in 11 of 12 model-task settings, by 3.9 percentage points on average, while generally maintaining higher token entropy.
items.tldr: VRSD (Verbal Regularization Self-Distillation) améliore l'auto-distillation des LLM en régulant l'influence des informations privilégiées (PI) pour éviter les biais de raisonnement, augmentant le Pass@1 de +3.9 points en moyenne. Pertinent pour le fine-tuning efficace et l'optimisation des modèles.
